messages:
sam: Heads-up: running a planned dry-run tonight at 00:30 UTC for the spot GPU fallback flow. Goal: validate automated failover to reserved pools and telemetry for cost/regressions. Will simulate 2x spot evictions in us-west1 and one partial network blackhole in the same region.
priya: Ack. Can we keep the ML serving canary pinned to the nvidia-a100s in reserved so we can observe tail-latency changes?
miguel: +1. I’ll set the canary to model:stable:v2 on dedicated pool. Also will enable extra tracing for kv-cache hit rates.
jordan: What are the success criteria? I assume: (1) no 5xxs above baseline, (2) SLO for p99 latency within 15% of baseline, (3) no data-plane leaks to prod-only networks.
sam: Correct. Add: autoscaler should spin up reserved instances within target 90s, fallback routing to cheaper model variant is allowed but should be logged and metric-tagged.
lee: I updated the runbook with the sequence: 1) ops-bot will trigger synthetic evictions, 2) autoscaler responds, 3) routing layer switches, 4) smoke tests run, 5) rollback. I left the terraform plan snippet in the runbook for the reserved pool:
```
resource "redwood_reserved_pool" " reserved_us_west_gpu" {
  region = "us-west1"
  gpu_type = "a100"
  min_instances = 4
  max_instances = 16
}
```
priya: Ops-bot, please confirm prechecks: cluster-health >= 95%, schedulable capacity >= 6 GPUs, and no pending infra changes.
ops-bot: prechecks: cluster-health=98%, schedulable-gpus=12, pending-migrations=0, k8s-version=1.26. Autoscaler-config=stable. Proceed window open: 00:30-01:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:
miguel: I’ll prepare the synthetic clients that flood small-batch chat requests to surface latency regressions. Keep QPS at ~120 per cluster.
jordan: During the run, if we see >3% error spike, we abort and collect diagnostics: full profiling from runtime, network flow logs, and container-level logs. Who triggers abort? Priya (oncall) or Sam (eng lead).
priya: I'll be oncall. Abort criteria acknowledged.
sam: Starting now: first eviction in us-west1-a in 60s. Will post step ticks.
ops-bot: action: simulate-eviction region=us-west1-a count=1 type=spot_simulation ts=1782467950
lee: Eviction observed by scheduler; 1 job drained, fallback routing kicked in to dedicated pool; trace-id=t8f3.
miguel: KV cache warmup looks ok — hit-rate dipped 8% for 30s, recovered within 2mins. No 5xxs on canary.
jordan: p99 latency +9% at peak, within the 15% window. Good. Noting request retry counts increased by 0.2 req/sec.
priya: Running second eviction now in us-west1-b.
ops-bot: action: simulate-eviction region=us-west1-b count=1 type=spot_simulation ts=1782468060
lee: Autoscaler launched 3 reserved nodes, time-to-ready=78s. All pods scheduled.
miguel: Smoke tests: all text-gen endpoints returned 200. Model degradation checks show top-k match >98% for eval set.
jordan: Observed a small networking flap between AZs during the second eviction, manifested as transient TCP resets at 00:41:00 UTC, lasted ~45s. No flow leak to private subnets.
priya: Marking this as a partial network blackhole observed. Ops-bot, capture VPC flow logs + route table snapshot for the window.
ops-bot: archived logs: s3://redwood-ops/eviction-dryrun/1782467890/flows.log ; routes: s3://redwood-ops/eviction-dryrun/1782467890/routes.json
sam: Final check: error rate stayed at baseline, p99 within target, autoscaler met 90s SLA (78s), fallback routing logged. Overall: PASS with notes (network flap).
jordan: Action items: 1) add AZ-to-AZ TCP reset detector to ops alerts, 2) tighten autoscaler warmup config to prefer pre-warmed images (reduce cold boot by ~10s), 3) add a canary to verify kv-cache warmup on new nodes.
lee: I’ll open Jira tickets for each: INFRA-2334, INFRA-2335, INFRA-2336.
priya: Great run. We should schedule a follow-up retro with product owners to discuss cost impact of keeping slightly higher reserved min_instances.
sam: Thanks team. Saving run artifacts and notes under the run folder. :tada:
